entities.name: Armenian Communist Party
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Communist Party of Armenia (Hayastani Komunistakan Kusaktsutyun), which governed Soviet Armenia from 1921 to 1990 — the entire Soviet period — as the sole legal party, was the institutional vehicle through which Soviet power organized, controlled, and developed the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic. The party oversaw both Soviet Armenia's worst moments (Stalinist purges, collectivization, population deportations) and its most productive (industrialization, universal education, cultural flourishing through Armenian-language institutions).

Soviet Armenia was established in 1920-1921 after Bolshevik forces overthrew the First Armenian Republic. The Armenian Communist Party, under Moscow's control, implemented collectivization (destroying the Armenian peasantry's traditional agriculture), industrialized Armenia (creating Yerevan's industrial base), and managed the Stalinist purges of the 1930s that killed thousands of Armenian intellectuals, party leaders, and ordinary citizens. Anastas Mikoyan (a Georgian-born Armenian) was among the most powerful Soviet leaders of the Stalin era, serving as a CP Armenia leader before his Moscow career.

Under Mikhail Gorbachev's glasnost and perestroika, the Armenian Communist Party was challenged by the Armenian National Movement (HHSh), which swept to power in 1990 elections. Armenia declared independence in 1991; the Communist Party was suspended and renamed but continued as a marginal political force. Post-independence Armenia has been dominated by the HHSh and later the Republican Party and My Step Alliance — the Communist Party having lost its Soviet-era monopoly and finding no significant mass constituency in independent Armenia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Armenian Communist Party — governing Soviet Armenia for 70 years through Stalinist terror, industrialization, and cultural policy, producing Soviet leaders of national importance, and being peacefully displaced by the independence movement — is a central institution in the making and unmaking of Soviet Armenia.
